Local structured priors for `1B` were empty, so this chapter rests on narrative and primary/independent sources only. I reused only the sources that genuinely bear on nuclear and existential-risk responsibility.

**Reused evidence**
- `E0008` [Chapter 4. The President of the Russian Federation](https://www.constitution.ru/en/10003000-05.htm) | exact lenses: `1B.3`, `1B.4`, `1B.7`, `1B.8`, `1B.10`
- `E0003` [President of Russia](https://en.kremlin.ru/structure/president) | exact lenses: `1B.3`, `1B.7`, `1B.10`
- `E0011` [Putin warns West of risk of nuclear war, says Moscow can strike Western targets](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-warns-west-of-risk-of-nuclear-war-says-moscow-can-strike-western-targets-3319714) | exact lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.5`, `1B.8`

**New evidence**
- [Putin, in rare US interview, says Russia has no interest in wider war](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-in-rare-us-interview-says-russia-has-no-interest-in-attacking-poland-or-latvia-3298168) | Reuters | 2024-02-08/09 | direct claim: Putin said Russia had no interest in expanding the war to Poland or Latvia and was open to dialogue; the article quotes his denial of wider-war intent. | source type: wire reporting on direct interview; high credibility for attribution, low for sincerity. | period fit: early-2024 crisis context. | ruler attribution: direct Putin statement, but self-serving and strategic. | limitations/contrary points: the same interview also reaffirmed war aims and pressure on Ukraine; not evidence of restraint in doctrine or force posture. | lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.5`, `1B.8`
- [Putin warns West of risk of nuclear war, says Moscow can strike Western targets](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-warns-west-of-risk-of-nuclear-war-says-moscow-can-strike-western-targets-3319714) | Reuters | 2024-02-29 | direct claim: Putin warned that sending NATO troops to Ukraine risked nuclear war and said Russia could strike Western targets; he also claimed openness to strategic-stability talks. | source type: wire reporting on a major address; high credibility. | period fit: pre-inauguration but within the 2024 ruler-period. | ruler attribution: direct Putin rhetoric from the Federal Assembly address. | limitations/contrary points: the “talks” line is offset by explicit nuclear threats and strike language. | lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.5`, `1B.8`, `1B.10`
- [Putin orders tactical nuclear weapon drills to deter the West](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-orders-tactical-nuclear-weapon-drills-to-deter-the-west--defence-ministry-3419973) | Reuters | 2024-05-06 | direct claim: Russia announced tactical-nuclear deployment drills after what it called Western threats. | source type: wire reporting on official military announcement; high credibility. | period fit: during the first months of Putin’s new term. | ruler attribution: Putin ordered the exercise; not actual use, but deliberate signaling. | limitations/contrary points: Kremlin described it as exercise/ deterrence, not operational deployment; still escalatory. | lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.5`, `1B.8`
- [Putin says Russia does not need to use nuclear weapons for victory in Ukraine](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-russia-does-not-need-to-use-nuclear-weapons-for-victory-in-ukraine-3475651) | Reuters | 2024-06-07 | direct claim: Putin said Russia had no need to use nuclear weapons to secure victory in Ukraine and framed that as the strongest signal yet against escalation. | source type: wire reporting on direct Putin remarks; high credibility. | period fit: mid-2024 wartime signaling. | ruler attribution: direct Putin statement. | limitations/contrary points: this is rhetorical restraint, not evidence of arms-control progress; it sits alongside Belarus deployment and later doctrine hardening. | lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.8`
- [Putin Says Russia Positions Nuclear Bombs in Belarus As Warning to West](https://tolonews.com/world-183810) | Reuters | 2024-06-07 | direct claim: Putin said the first Russian tactical nuclear warheads had been delivered to Belarus and that the transfer would be completed by year-end. | source type: wire reporting of ruler statement; high credibility for attribution, low for independent verification. | period fit: decisive 2024 posture change. | ruler attribution: direct Putin decision and public claim. | limitations/contrary points: Belarus deployment was not conclusively verified by independent observers; NPT/legal questions remained. | lenses: `1B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.10`
- [Russia begins second stage of tactical nuclear weapon drills with Belarus](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-begins-second-stage-of-tactical-nuclear-weapon-drills-with-belarus-3478894) | Reuters | 2024-06-11 | direct claim: Russia and Belarus continued tactical-nuclear drills, practicing deployment procedures after earlier stages ordered by Putin. | source type: wire reporting on military exercise; high credibility. | period fit: confirms this was not a one-off rhetorical event. | ruler attribution: ordered/hosted under Putin’s deterrence posture. | limitations/contrary points: a drill is not use; Kremlin framed it as routine readiness. | lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.3`, `1B.5`, `1B.8`
- [Putin issues nuclear warning to the West over strikes on Russia from Ukraine](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-issues-nuclear-warning-to-the-west-over-strikes-on-russia-from-ukraine-3632764) | Reuters | 2024-09-25 | direct claim: Putin said Russia could use nuclear weapons if struck with conventional missiles and would treat a conventional strike supported by a nuclear power as a joint attack. | source type: wire reporting on Security Council remarks; high credibility. | period fit: central 2024 doctrine shift. | ruler attribution: direct Putin initiative and public warning. | limitations/contrary points: Kremlin framed the move as deterrence against Western escalation; the practical military threshold was still broadening. | lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.4`, `1B.5`, `1B.8`, `1B.10`
- [Executive Order Approving the Basic Principles of State Policy of the Russian Federation on Nuclear Deterrence](https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/75598) | President of Russia | 2024-11-19 | direct claim: Putin signed a new nuclear-deterrence decree, revoked the 2020 version, and said it specifies when Russia may use nuclear weapons. | source type: primary official decree summary; very high credibility for the act, low for self-justifying interpretation. | period fit: end-of-2024 institutionalization of the new posture. | ruler attribution: direct presidential action with immediate force. | limitations/contrary points: the text is formal doctrine, not proof of prudence; it codifies broader use conditions. | lenses: `1B.3`, `1B.4`, `1B.5`, `1B.7`, `1B.10`
- [Russia fires missiles to simulate 'massive' response to a nuclear attack](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-orders-strategic-nuclear-training-exercise-3688362) | Reuters | 2024-10-29 | direct claim: Putin kicked off a strategic nuclear exercise with practical launches; he said nuclear use is a last resort and Russia would not enter a new arms race. | source type: wire reporting on live exercise and Putin remarks; high credibility. | period fit: late-2024 escalation-management evidence. | ruler attribution: direct Putin command over strategic-deterrence forces. | limitations/contrary points: the drill simulated a massive retaliation scenario and increased coercive pressure even while claiming restraint. | lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.3`, `1B.8`
- [Nuclear Notebook: Russian Nuclear Weapons 2025](https://fas.org/publication-term/nuclear-notebook/) | Federation of American Scientists | 2025-05-06 | direct claim: Russia’s 2024 nuclear arsenal was still immense; nonstrategic warheads stayed relatively stable, but 2024 saw several high-profile exercises and upgrades to a suspected nuclear storage depot in Belarus. | source type: technical independent analysis; high credibility. | period fit: retrospective but explicitly summarizes 2024. | ruler attribution: describes posture and modernization under Putin’s 2024 control. | limitations/contrary points: force levels did not visibly jump in open sources, which tempers claims of a major quantitative expansion. | lenses: `1B.3`, `1B.5`, `1B.10`
- [6. World nuclear forces](https://www.sipri.org/yearbook/2025/06) | SIPRI | 2025 | direct claim: Russia updated its official doctrine in November 2024, apparently expanding contingencies for nuclear use; Russia and Belarus both claimed deployment of Russian nuclear weapons in Belarus, but SIPRI says there was no conclusive evidence. | source type: independent technical analysis; very high credibility. | period fit: retrospective summary of 2024. | ruler attribution: directly relevant to Putin’s 2024 doctrine choices. | limitations/contrary points: no conclusive external verification of Belarus deployment. | lenses: `1B.4`, `1B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.10`
- [8. Nuclear disarmament, arms control, non-proliferation and security](https://www.sipri.org/yearbook/2025/08) | SIPRI | 2025 | direct claim: by end-2024 nuclear disarmament was more elusive than at any point since the cold war, and strategic dialogue between Russia and the United States had effectively ceased. | source type: independent policy/technical analysis; very high credibility. | period fit: structural year-end assessment. | ruler attribution: not Putin alone, but strongly tied to his 2024 posture and choices. | limitations/contrary points: this is system-level context, not a single ruler act. | lenses: `1B.4`, `1B.10`
- [Prospect of Nuclear Accident ‘Dangerously Close’ at Zaporizhzhia Power Plant in Ukraine](https://press.un.org/en/2024/sc15662.doc.htm) | UN Security Council / IAEA | 2024-04-15 | direct claim: Grossi warned the prospect of a nuclear accident at Zaporizhzhia was “dangerously close” after attacks on the plant. | source type: primary UN/IAEA record; very high credibility. | period fit: core 2024 existential-risk evidence. | ruler attribution: the plant was under Russian occupation and military control in Putin’s war. | limitations/contrary points: the UN note does not alone assign every attack to Moscow, and Ukraine disputed responsibility. | lenses: `1B.5`, `1B.9`, `1B.10`
- [Russian Military Actions at Ukraine’s Nuclear Power Plants](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/IN11883.html) | Congressional Research Service | 2024-04-12 | direct claim: Russia’s occupation of Zaporizhzhia and April 2024 drone strikes escalated nuclear-safety and security dangers; the US called for Russia to withdraw personnel. | source type: congressional research summary of official/technical record; high credibility. | period fit: contemporaneous 2024 safety assessment. | ruler attribution: the occupation and militarization are attributable to Putin’s war policy. | limitations/contrary points: CRS is a secondary synthesis, not a field inspection. | lenses: `1B.5`, `1B.9`, `1B.10`
- [Ukraine and Russia swap accusations over fire at Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/ukraine-and-russia-swap-accusations-over-fire-at-zaporizhzhia-nuclear-plant-3565986) | Reuters | 2024-08-12 | direct claim: smoke and blasts at the Russian-occupied plant again triggered IAEA warnings that reckless attacks endanger nuclear safety. | source type: wire reporting with IAEA attribution; high credibility. | period fit: mid-2024 risk persistence. | ruler attribution: again tied to Russian occupation and wartime control, though immediate causation was contested. | limitations/contrary points: both sides blamed each other; no radiological release was reported. | lenses: `1B.5`, `1B.9`, `1B.10`
- [Analysis-With defence pledge, Putin makes shift towards North Korea](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/analysiswith-defence-pledge-putin-makes-shift-towards-north-korea-3489078) and [Putin says Russia may deliver weapons to North Korea](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-russia-is-considering-changing-its-nuclear-doctrine-3490550) | Reuters | 2024-06-19 / 2024-06-20 | direct claim: Putin signed a mutual-defence pact with North Korea and then said Russia might supply weapons to Pyongyang as a mirror response to Western arming of Ukraine. | source type: wire reporting on diplomacy and follow-on remarks; high credibility. | period fit: important late-June alignment with a nuclear-armed state. | ruler attribution: direct Putin foreign-policy choice. | limitations/contrary points: the pact is not itself a nuclear-transfer agreement, but it deepens alignment with a nuclear-armed regime and raises escalation risk. | lenses: `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.10`

**Search and rejection summary**
- I considered roughly 30 documents across Kremlin primary pages, Reuters wire reporting, SIPRI, FAS, UN/IAEA, CRS, AP, and a few regional republishers.
- I collapsed Reuters syndications and near-duplicates into one retained URL per distinct claim, so I did not keep multiple republications of the same story unless they added a materially different fact.
- I rejected out-of-period or low-value context such as the 2020 doctrine text, 2023 Belarus background, generic 2024 election results, broad rights reporting, economy coverage, Crocus coverage, and Kursk reporting when they did not add anything direct to nuclear/existential-risk responsibility.
- I also rejected several blocked or timeout-prone Kremlin transcript opens; where the official Kremlin page was inaccessible, I used the accessible official decree summary or Reuters coverage of the same dated event.
- I rejected repeated Belarus/North Korea items when they only restated the same core claim without adding a new risk-bearing choice by Putin.

**Remaining gaps**
- Belarus tactical-warhead deployment in 2024 is still not independently confirmed in open sources; I have Putin’s claim, allied drill evidence, and SIPRI/FAS discussion, but not conclusive verification.
- Internal command-and-control discipline, custody arrangements, and accident-prevention safeguards remain largely opaque.
- Backchannel crisis management with Washington/NATO is underdocumented publicly, so de-escalation claims are hard to test beyond Putin’s own rhetoric.
- The ZNPP risk record is strong on danger, but the exact causal chain for each incident remains disputed in open reporting.

If you want the next step, I can turn this into a chapter-ready evidence dossier keyed lens-by-lens for `1B.1` through `1B.10`, still without scoring.
